title: Module 5 Interpretation Check
intro: Each item gives you a short research situation. Decide what the evidence supports.

items.q: A population has sigma = 10. What is the standard error for samples of n = 64?
items.why: SE = 10 divided by the square root of 64, which is 10/8 = 1.25.

items.q: Population mean is 25, sigma = 10, and n = 64. A sample has M = 27.5. What is its z score?
Scores in a skewed population have mean 100 and SD 15. For samples of n = 4 and n = 100, in which case are the sample means more normally distributed?
items.why: The central limit theorem applies more strongly as n grows.

items.q: Which sample mean is more surprising if the population mean is 100 and sigma is 15?
items.why: With n = 36, SE = 2.5 and z = 3.2. With n = 9, SE = 5 and z = 1.6. The same difference is more surprising with a larger sample.

items.q: A researcher says, "My sample SD was 12, so the standard error is 12." What is the error?
o: The standard error is the SD divided by the square root of n, not the SD itself
The standard error is the variance
items.why: The standard error is smaller than the SD whenever n exceeds 1.
